title: Janda's Crossed Syndromes and Kendall's Postures — Tight, Weak and What To Do

hook.en: Some muscles shorten, others weaken, and together they draw a recognisable pattern. Learn the upper and lower crossed syndromes, the four Kendall postures and how to turn a pattern into a treatment plan.
hook.ur: Kuch muscles chhote ho jate hain, kuch kamzor, aur milkar ek pehchane jane wala pattern banate hain. Upper aur lower crossed syndromes, Kendall ki chaar postures aur pattern ko treatment plan mein badalna seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll name the tight and weak muscles of the upper and lower crossed syndromes, identify the four Kendall spinal postures and plan treatment that fits the findings.
goal.ur: End tak aap upper aur lower crossed syndromes ke tight aur weak muscles batayenge, Kendall ki chaar spinal postures pehchanenge aur findings se milta ilaaj plan karenge.

text.en: Vladimir Janda described two common patterns in which tight muscles and weak muscles **cross** each other. In the **upper crossed syndrome** the tight upper trapezius, levator scapulae and pectoralis (front) cross the weak deep neck flexors, lower trapezius and serratus anterior (back): you see forward head, rounded shoulders and a kyphotic upper back. In the **lower crossed syndrome** the tight hip flexors and lumbar extensors cross the weak abdominals and gluteals: you see an anterior pelvic tilt and increased lumbar lordosis.
text.ur: Vladimir Janda ne do aam patterns bataye jahan tight aur weak muscles ek doosre ko **cross** karte hain. **Upper crossed syndrome** mein tight upper trapezius, levator scapulae aur pectoralis (samne) kamzor deep neck flexors, lower trapezius aur serratus anterior (peechay) ko cross karte hain: forward head, rounded shoulders aur kyphotic upper back nazar aati hai. **Lower crossed syndrome** mein tight hip flexors aur lumbar extensors kamzor abdominals aur gluteals ko cross karte hain: anterior pelvic tilt aur barhi hui lumbar lordosis nazar aati hai.

text.en: Picture an X. One diagonal is a pair of tight muscles pulling the body forward and down; the other diagonal is a pair of weak muscles that should hold it back and up. The body settles where the strong diagonal wins — a rounded, tilted shape. Treatment loosens the tight diagonal and trains the weak diagonal.
text.ur: X ka tasawwur karein. Ek diagonal tight muscles ki jori hai jo jism ko aage aur neeche kheench rahi hai; doosra diagonal kamzor muscles ki jori hai jo usay peechay aur upar rakhe. Jism wahan tikta hai jahan mazboot diagonal jeet jata hai — gol, tilted shakal. Ilaaj tight diagonal ko dheela karta hai aur kamzor diagonal ko train karta hai.

intro.en: See the pattern on the patient: forward head, rounded shoulders and the pelvic tilt. Use the beats to move from the posture to the muscles that cause it. The labels name the **short/tight** and **long/weak** muscles for each pattern.
intro.ur: Mareez par pattern dekhein: forward head, rounded shoulders aur pelvic tilt. Beats se posture se un muscles tak jayein jo isay banate hain. Labels har pattern ke **chhote/tight** aur **lambay/kamzor** muscles ke naam batate hain.

question.en: A desk worker has forward head, rounded shoulders and tight pectorals. Which muscles are most likely weak?
question.ur: Desk worker ka sar aage, shoulders gol aur pectorals tight hain. Kaun se muscles sab se zyada kamzor hone ka imkaan?

text.en: Deep neck flexors, lower trapezius and serratus anterior
text.ur: Deep neck flexors, lower trapezius aur serratus anterior

feedback.en: Yes — that is the upper crossed pattern: tight front, weak back. Treat both sides of the cross.
feedback.ur: Haan — yeh upper crossed pattern hai: samne tight, peechay kamzor. Cross ke dono hissay ka ilaaj karein.

feedback.en: Those are the tight, overactive muscles.

intro.en: Increased thoracic kyphosis with an **anterior pelvic tilt** and increased lumbar lordosis: the lower crossed syndrome. Watch the pelvis tilt forward and the lumbar curve deepen. The hip flexors and lumbar extensors are tight; abdominals and gluteals are weak.
intro.ur: Barha hua thoracic kyphosis aur **anterior pelvic tilt** aur barhi hui lumbar lordosis: lower crossed syndrome. Pelvis ko aage tilt aur lumbar curve ko gehra hota dekhein. Hip flexors aur lumbar extensors tight; abdominals aur gluteals kamzor.

intro.en: The pelvis shifts forward of the plumb line and tilts back; the trunk leans backward. Hamstrings and upper abdominals are strong and short; hip flexors, external obliques and neck flexors are weak and long. Notice how different it is from the kypho-lordotic pattern.
intro.ur: Pelvis plumb line se aage shift aur peechay tilt hota hai; trunk peechay jhukta hai. Hamstrings aur upper abdominals mazboot aur chhote; hip flexors, external obliques aur neck flexors kamzor aur lambay. Dekhein yeh kypho-lordotic pattern se kitna mukhtalif hai.

text.en: **Stretching what looks tight without testing it.** A rounded shoulder may be a short pectoralis minor, but it can also be a tight posterior capsule, a stiff thoracic spine or weak scapular stabilisers. Test muscle length (pectoralis minor index, Thomas test) and strength (lower trapezius, serratus anterior) before choosing, and re-test the same finding after treatment. Remember also that a pattern is a **tendency**, not a diagnosis, and every patient does not follow it.
text.ur: **Jo tight lagta hai usay test kiye bagair stretch karna.** Gol shoulder chhota pectoralis minor ho sakta hai, lekin tight posterior capsule, sakht thoracic spine ya kamzor scapular stabilisers bhi ho sakte hain. Chunne se pehle muscle length (pectoralis minor index, Thomas test) aur strength (lower trapezius, serratus anterior) test karein, aur ilaaj ke baad wohi finding dobara test karein. Yeh bhi yaad rakhein ke pattern ek **rujhan** hai, tashkhees nahi, aur har mareez is ko follow nahi karta.

question.en: In which posture do the hamstrings and upper abdominals tend to be strong and short, while the hip flexors are weak?
question.ur: Kis posture mein hamstrings aur upper abdominals mazboot aur chhote jabke hip flexors kamzor hote hain?

feedback.en: Yes — the pelvis shifts forward and the hips hang in extension on strong hamstrings; it is the opposite of the lower crossed pattern.
feedback.ur: Haan — pelvis aage shift hota hai aur hips mazboot hamstrings par extension mein latakte hain; yeh lower crossed pattern ka ulta hai.

feedback.en: There the hip flexors are tight, not weak.
feedback.ur: Wahan hip flexors tight hain, kamzor nahi.

feedback.en: That concerns the neck and shoulder girdle.
feedback.ur: Yeh gardan aur shoulder girdle ka masla hai.

text.en: **Build the plan from the cross.** For the upper crossed syndrome: stretch pectoralis minor and upper trapezius, **teach scapular setting**, then strengthen lower trapezius, serratus anterior and deep neck flexors (craniocervical flexion). For the lower crossed syndrome: stretch hip flexors, strengthen glutes and abdominals with pelvic-control exercises, and address work habits (long sitting). Measure the change: occiput-to-wall, craniovertebral angle, Thomas test, plank or bridge endurance.
text.ur: **Cross se plan banayein.** Upper crossed syndrome ke liye: pectoralis minor aur upper trapezius ko stretch karein, **scapular setting sikhayein**, phir lower trapezius, serratus anterior aur deep neck flexors (craniocervical flexion) ko strengthen karein. Lower crossed syndrome ke liye: hip flexors stretch, glutes aur abdominals ko pelvic-control exercises se strengthen, aur kaam ki aadatein (der tak baithna) theek karein. Tabdeeli naapein: occiput-to-wall, craniovertebral angle, Thomas test, plank ya bridge endurance.

text.en: The crossed-syndrome model is **clinically useful but weakly supported by research**: studies find inconsistent relationships between these muscle imbalances and pain, and many pain-free people show the pattern. The best-supported approach is to treat what you can measure in the patient (lost range, weakness, pain that changes with position) rather than a label, and to use exercise and graded loading instead of stretching alone.
text.ur: Crossed-syndrome model **clinically useful lekin research se kamzor taur par mehfooz** hai: studies in muscle imbalances aur dard ke beech be-tarteeb taluq paati hain, aur bohat se dard se azad log yeh pattern dikhate hain. Sab se behtar tareeqa woh hai jo aap patient mein naap sakte hain (kami hui range, kamzori, position se badalta dard) us ka ilaaj karna na ke label ka, aur akeli stretching ke bajaye exercise aur graded loading use karna.

question.en: Why might strengthening alone work better than stretching alone for a rounded-shoulder posture?
question.ur: Gol shoulder posture ke liye sirf strengthening sirf stretching se behtar kyun ho sakti hai?

answer.en: Because the problem is often a weak, under-active lower trapezius and serratus anterior that cannot hold the scapula back and up, not a pectoralis that is too short to lengthen. Strengthening the weak group improves position and function; stretching a muscle that is not short adds nothing. Test first.
answer.ur: Kyunke masla aksar kamzor, under-active lower trapezius aur serratus anterior ka hota hai jo scapula ko peechay aur upar nahi pakar sakte, aisa pectoralis nahi jo lamba karne ke liye bohat chhota ho. Kamzor group ko strengthen karne se position aur function behtar hota hai; jo muscle chhota nahi usay stretch karne se kuch nahi milta. Pehle test karein.

question.en: What is the best evidence-based attitude toward the crossed-syndrome model?
question.ur: Crossed-syndrome model ke baare mein sab se behtar evidence-based rawaiyya kaun sa hai?

text.en: Use it as a hypothesis, test the muscles in the patient and treat measurable deficits
text.ur: Isay hypothesis ki tarah use karein, patient mein muscles test karein aur naapi ja sakne wali kamiyon ka ilaaj karein

feedback.en: Yes — it guides your examination but does not replace it.
feedback.ur: Haan — yeh aap ke examination ki rehnumai karta hai lekin usay badalta nahi.

text.en: Apply it to every patient with poor posture
text.ur: Har kharab posture wale mareez par lagayein

feedback.en: Not every patient follows the pattern.
feedback.ur: Har mareez pattern follow nahi karta.

feedback.en: It is a useful clinical map when tested.
feedback.ur: Test karne par yeh kaam ka clinical naqsha hai.

text.en: **Refer** if a posture change is new and painful with weight loss, fever, night pain, or neurological symptoms (cord or tumour), if a child has progressive spinal deformity, or if an older adult has sudden height loss or thoracic pain (fracture). Do not stretch or manipulate into a painful, fixed posture.
text.ur: **Refer karein** agar posture mein tabdeeli nayi ho aur dardnak ho, wazan ghatna, bukhar, raat ka dard ya neurological symptoms (cord ya tumour) ke saath, agar bachay mein spinal deformity barh rahi ho, ya buzurg mein achanak qad kam hona ya thoracic dard (fracture) ho. Dardnak, fixed posture mein stretch ya manipulate na karein.

summary.en: Upper crossed = tight upper trapezius, levator, pectorals and weak deep neck flexors, lower trapezius, serratus; lower crossed = tight hip flexors and lumbar extensors and weak abdominals and glutes.
summary.ur: Upper crossed = tight upper trapezius, levator, pectorals aur kamzor deep neck flexors, lower trapezius, serratus; lower crossed = tight hip flexors aur lumbar extensors aur kamzor abdominals aur glutes.

summary.en: Know Kendall's four postures (kypho-lordotic, lordotic, sway-back, flat-back) and test muscles before treating.
summary.ur: Kendall ki chaar postures (kypho-lordotic, lordotic, sway-back, flat-back) jaanein aur ilaaj se pehle muscles test karein.

summary.en: Treat measurable deficits with stretching, scapular and pelvic control and strengthening; the model is a hypothesis, not a diagnosis.
summary.ur: Naapi ja sakne wali kamiyon ka ilaaj stretching, scapular aur pelvic control aur strengthening se karein; model hypothesis hai, tashkhees nahi.

front.en: Which muscles are tight in the upper crossed syndrome?
front.ur: Upper crossed syndrome mein kaun se muscles tight hain?

back.en: Upper trapezius, levator scapulae, pectoralis major and minor (and sternocleidomastoid).
back.ur: Upper trapezius, levator scapulae, pectoralis major aur minor (aur sternocleidomastoid).

front.en: Which muscles are weak in the lower crossed syndrome?
front.ur: Lower crossed syndrome mein kaun se muscles kamzor hain?

back.en: Abdominals and gluteus maximus and medius.
back.ur: Abdominals aur gluteus maximus aur medius.

front.en: How does sway-back posture differ from kypho-lordotic?
front.ur: Sway-back posture kypho-lordotic se kaise mukhtalif hai?

back.en: Sway-back: pelvis forward and tilted back, trunk leaning back, strong short hamstrings; kypho-lordotic: anterior pelvic tilt with tight hip flexors.
back.ur: Sway-back: pelvis aage aur peechay tilted, trunk peechay, mazboot chhote hamstrings; kypho-lordotic: tight hip flexors ke saath anterior pelvic tilt.

front.en: How good is the evidence for the crossed-syndrome model?
front.ur: Crossed-syndrome model ka evidence kitna acha hai?

back.en: Weak and inconsistent: use it as a hypothesis and treat measurable findings.
back.ur: Kamzor aur be-tarteeb: isay hypothesis ki tarah use karein aur naapi ja sakne wali findings ka ilaaj karein.
